systemic: Style clash everywhere: pixel-scaled game textures at varying texel sizes (roughly 6-14 screen px per texel) are mixed with flat vector PIL shapes (trees, towers, anvils, pumpjack, campfire, sun). There is no single rendering language.
Sticker lineups: rows of item sprites on a rail or shelf along the bottom (copper, bronze, steel, IE, storage, food) read as an inventory dump rather than a scene.
Glow halos around single giant sprites (thermometer, totem, swords, gauge, hammer) give a pasted-sticker look.
No shared light or ground: objects float, have no shadows or contact, and light directions differ (planets, glows).
Clip-art motifs repeat across chapters: line-ray sun (welcome, climate, farming, explore), the same tower (welcome, explore), anvil and lantern variants.
Top band often just faint hazy mountains and bottom/right areas empty or muddy (copper, bronze, steel, welcome, tfmg).
Objects clipped by the screen edge (windmill, ringed planet, pylons, backpack, moon).

Readability: narrow section panels shrink header text until it can't be read (health s2, farming s3/s5, storage s2, mekanism s2/s4, explore s2/s5, twilight s2, steel s3, pneumatic s4/s5, bronze s4/s5, copper s3). Node lines and panels are otherwise clear over the art.
Red valve rings and dotted particles read as UI errors or dirt.
ceiling_estimate: About 7.5, with 8 possible for the best chapters (food, create, twilight, space) after strict cleanup. 9 is not realistic with procedural PIL motifs plus upscaled item textures composed by fractions. A 9 needs one coherent rendering style with intentional lighting, depth, and hand-placed detail, and generic geometric motifs can't supply that. They will always read as clip-art next to real Minecraft pixel art. Biggest gains from cheapest to most expensive: (1) pick one medium, preferably pure pixel art at one fixed integer texel scale, and redraw or drop the vector props; (2) remove lineups, oversize glow stickers and clip-art suns; (3) add a shared light/ground pass (contact shadows, rim light from the hero light source); (4) fix the header-text shrink. Reaching 9 would take hand-pixelled or commissioned per-chapter illustrations (or block-built in-game dioramas rendered as screenshots) used as the scene layer.
